result.title: TSIR: Ray-Traced Triangle Splats for Inverse Rendering
result.summary: Inverse rendering enables realistic relighting for visual effects and augmented reality. However, overlapping Gaussian primitives complicate surface recovery and require costly multi-layer traversal and compositing for light transport. We propose TSIR, a two-stage inverse rendering method that reconstructs relightable triangle splats from multi-view images. The first stage prepares opaque triangle splats with learnable vertex shading normals. The second stage directly traces these surfaces to estimate materials through Monte Carlo integration of direct illumination and indirect reflections, reducing reliance on multi-layer compositing. Anti-aliasing improves rendering quality while maintaining efficiency. Experiments demonstrate higher relighting quality than the evaluated baselines and more efficient anti-aliasing than supersampling.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 TSIR，一种两阶段逆渲染方法：先从多视图图像重建可重光照的三角形 splats，再直接追踪这些表面以估计材质并实现重光照。
